g.text: COMPLEX LINE INTEGRALS & CAUCHY'S INTEGRAL THEOREMS ENGINE
Parametric Line Integrals // Cauchy-Goursat Principle // Cauchy's Integral Formula & Higher Derivatives // Multi-Pole Splitting
GATE 2027 TITANS ENGINE
SPEC: ULTRA-HD 4K BLUEPRINT
01. COMPLEX CONTOUR INTEGRATION & CANONICAL CIRCLE INTEGRAL
Parametric definition // Real Riemann decomposition // The fundamental winding integral
PARAMETRIC CONTOUR INTEGRAL FORMULATION
Let C be a smooth curve parametrized by z(t) = x(t) + i y(t) for t ∈ [a, b]:
∫ᶜ f(z) dz = ∫ᵢᵇ f(z(t)) z'(t) dt
∫ᶜ (u + iv)(dx + i dy) = ∫ᶜ (u dx - v dy) + i ∫ᶜ (v dx + u dy)
CORE INTEGRATION PROPERTIES:
• Linearity: ∫ [α f(z) + β g(z)] dz = α ∫ f(z) dz + β ∫ g(z) dz
• Orientation Reversal: ∫₋ᶜ f(z) dz = - ∫ᶜ f(z) dz
THE FUNDAMENTAL CIRCLE WINDING THEOREM
Integrate (z - z₀)ⁿ along circle C: |z - z₀| = R (counterclockwise, z = z₀ + R eᵢṤ):
∮ᶜ (z - z₀)ⁿ dz =
2π i (if n = -1)
Proof: ∫₀²ᵖ Rⁿ eᵢⁿṤ (i R eᵢṤ dθ) = i Rⁿ⁺¹ ∫₀²ᵖ eᵢ(ⁿ⁺¹)Ṥ dθ = 2πi if n=-1 else 0!
★ The single most vital result in all of complex contour integration!
Serves as the foundation for both Cauchy's Integral Formula and Laurent series residues.
ML-INEQUALITY (CONTOUR INTEGRATION BOUNDING ENGINE)
THE ML-ESTIMATION THEOREM
|∫ᶜ f(z) dz| ≤ M · L
• L = Total arc length of curve C = ∫ᶜ |dz|
• M = Maximum value of |f(z)| on C: M = maxᶍ∈ᶜ |f(z)|
★ Indispensable for proving vanishing of semicircular arcs at infinity (R → ∞)!
GATE EXAM ESTIMATION APPLICATION
Estimate |∫ᶜ (e᷂ / (z² + 1)) dz| along semicircle C: |z| = R, Im(z) ≥ 0:
Length: L = π R
Denominator bound: |z² + 1| ≥ |z|² - 1 = R² - 1
Numerator bound: |e᷂| = eᵘ ≤ eⁿ (or e⁰ = 1 if Im(z)≥0)
Bound: |∫| ≤ πR / (R² - 1) → 0 as R → ∞ (Proves arc integral vanishes!)
02. CAUCHY-GOURSAT THEOREM & CONTOUR DEFORMATION
Zero loop integral in simply connected domains // Deformation of contours // Cross-cut theory
CAUCHY-GOURSAT THEOREM
∮ᶜ f(z) dz = 0
Condition: f(z) is analytic at ALL points on and inside simple closed contour C
PROOF VIA GREEN'S THEOREM IN THE PLANE:
∮ᶜ (u dx - v dy) + i ∮ᶜ (v dx + u dy) = ∬ᶑ (-vᵣ - uᵤ) dA + i ∬ᶑ (uᵣ - vᵤ) dA
By Cauchy-Riemann: uᵣ - vᵤ = 0 and -vᵣ - uᵤ = 0!
⇒ Both area integrals vanish identically ⇒ ∮ᶜ f(z) dz = 0!
Goursat's landmark contribution was proving this without assuming continuity of f'(z)!
PRINCIPLE OF CONTOUR DEFORMATION
HOMOTOPY / DEFORMATION THEOREM:
∮ᶜ₁ f(z) dz = ∮ᶜ₂ f(z) dz
Provided f(z) is analytic in the region bounded between C₁ and C₂!
MULTI-CONNECTED CROSS-CUT FORMULA:
∮ᶜ f(z) dz = ∮ᶜ₁ f(z) dz + ∮ᶜ₂ f(z) dz + ... + ∮ᶜₙ f(z) dz
Surrounding each isolated singularity with tiny circular sub-contours Cᵢ.
★ Enables replacing complicated contours (squares, ellipses) with simple circles!
PREPFUSION CLASSROOM DRILLS: INSTANT CAUCHY-GOURSAT ZERO TESTS
DRILL 1: ∮ᶜ e᷂ dz ALONG |z| = 2
f(z) = e᷂ is an entire function (analytic everywhere in ℂ).
No singularities exist anywhere in the complex plane.
INTEGRAL = 0
Solved by inspection in 2 seconds!
Same for ∮ sin z dz, ∮ cos z dz, ∮ z³ dz.
DRILL 2: ∮ᶜ 1/(z - 5) dz ALONG |z| = 2
Singularity of f(z) = 1/(z - 5) is at z = 5.
Contour is circle |z| = 2 (radius 2 centered at origin).
Point z = 5 lies strictly OUTSIDE contour!
INTEGRAL = 0
f(z) is analytic ON and INSIDE |z| = 2!
DRILL 3: ∮ᶜ (z² + 3)/(z² - 9) dz, |z| = 1
Singularities at z² - 9 = 0 ⇒ z = +3 and z = -3.
Contour is circle |z| = 1.
Both singularities lie strictly OUTSIDE contour!
INTEGRAL = 0
By Cauchy-Goursat theorem!
03. CAUCHY'S INTEGRAL FORMULA & N-TH DERIVATIVE ENGINE
Value at interior point from boundary data // Higher derivative generalization // Powerful shortcuts
CAUCHY'S INTEGRAL FORMULA (SIMPLE POLE AT z₀)
If f(z) is analytic on and inside simple closed contour C, and z₀ is INSIDE C:
f(z₀) = (1 / 2πi) ∮ᶜ [f(z) / (z - z₀)] dz
∮ᶜ [f(z) / (z - z₀)] dz = 2πi · f(z₀)
★ The integral is simply 2πi multiplied by the numerator evaluated at the singular point!
SPEED EXAMPLE: ∮ᶜ (e᷂ / (z - 1)) dz along |z| = 2
z₀ = 1 lies strictly inside |z| = 2. Numerator f(z) = e᷂ is analytic.
Answer = 2πi · f(1) = 2πi · e¹ = 2πe i (Solved in 5 seconds!)
CAUCHY'S DERIVATIVE FORMULA (POLE OF ORDER n+1)
For repeated poles of order (n + 1) in the denominator:
fⁿ(z₀) = (n! / 2πi) ∮ᶜ [f(z) / (z - z₀)ⁿ⁺¹] dz
∮ᶜ [f(z) / (z - z₀)ⁿ⁺¹] dz = (2πi / n!) · fⁿ(z₀)
⚠ Never forget to divide by n! (factorial) when calculating the integral!
SPEED DRILL: ∮ᶜ (e²᷂ / (z + 1)³) dz along |z| = 3
z₀ = -1 inside |z|=3. Order n + 1 = 3 ⇒ n = 2. f(z) = e²᷂ ⇒ f''(z) = 4e²᷂
Answer = (2πi / 2!) · 4e²(⁻¹) = πi · 4e⁻² = 4πe⁻² i
DEEP THEORETICAL CONSEQUENCES OF CAUCHY'S INTEGRAL FORMULAS
INFINITE DIFFERENTIABILITY
If f(z) is analytic, it possesses derivatives of ALL orders!
Remarkable contrast to real variables (where f'(x) being differentiable doesn't imply f''(x) exists!).
★ Once analytic, always smooth!
LIOUVILLE'S THEOREM
Every bounded entire function in ℂ MUST be constant!
If |f(z)| ≤ M for all z ∈ ℂ, then f'(z) = 0 everywhere.
★ Immediate proof that sin z, cos z, e᷂ cannot be bounded in ℂ!
MAXIMUM MODULUS PRINCIPLE
If f(z) is analytic in bounded domain D, |f(z)| achieves its maximum on the BOUNDARY of D.
Cannot have a local maximum in the interior unless f(z) is constant.
★ Crucial for stability in control theory!
04. MULTI-POLE SPLITTING & PARTIAL FRACTION ENGINE
Evaluating integrals with multiple singularities via partial fractions vs Cauchy formulas
DRILL 1: ∮ᶜ [1 / (z² + 4)] dz ALONG |z - i| = 2
Singularities at z² + 4 = 0 ⇒ z = 2i and z = -2i.
Check contour |z - i| = 2 (center = i, radius = 2):
CONTOUR INTERIOR AUDIT:
• For z = 2i: |2i - i| = |i| = 1 < 2 ⇒ INSIDE contour
• For z = -2i: |-2i - i| = |-3i| = 3 > 2 ⇒ OUTSIDE contour
REWRITE INTEGRAND IN CAUCHY FORM:
where f(z) = 1 / (z + 2i) is analytic inside C!
Answer = 2πi · f(2i) = 2πi · [1 / (2i + 2i)] = 2πi / 4i = π / 2
DRILL 2: ∮ᶜ [1 / (z² + 4)] dz ALONG |z| = 3
Both singularities z = +2i and z = -2i lie INSIDE |z| = 3.
METHOD: PARTIAL FRACTIONS SPLITTING
By Cauchy's theorem on each simple pole:
∮ᶜ [1/(z - 2i)] dz = 2πi and ∮ᶜ [1/(z + 2i)] dz = 2πi
★ Residues at 2i and -2i are 1/(4i) and -1/(4i); their sum is 0 ⇒ Integral = 0!
THE 3-STEP CANONICAL AUDIT FOR ANY CONTOUR INTEGRAL ∮ [P(z)/Q(z)] dz
STEP 1: LOCATE ALL ROOTS OF Q(z)=0
Find every singularity z₁, z₂, ..., zₙ.
Factor denominator completely.
Determine pole orders (powers).
STEP 2: FILTER BY CONTOUR REGION
Calculate distance |zᵢ - center|.
If distance < radius ⇒ KEEP (INSIDE)
If distance > radius ⇒ DISCARD (OUTSIDE)
STEP 3: EVALUATE & SUM
Apply Cauchy formula or Residue theorem:
Integral = 2πi · ∑ (Residues inside C)
Poles outside contribute EXACTLY ZERO!
